canal_p07_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_001.text: The fourteenth morning brought market boats from both directions, and Luo's toll counter looked unexpectedly prosperous. A pilot paid in copper warm from his palm; the next showed an annual crossing token with one month still valid. Yue began a receipt list beside the movement book. By the time she reached the third entry, she had mistaken a token check for fresh income. Pei tapped the empty cash space. A busy canal and a full cash box could look alike from a hopeful apprentice's first column.

canal_p07_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_002.text: Yue corrected the entry before adding any total. The token's payment belonged to its earlier receipt date, with present use recorded separately. Luo said most toll errors began with people wanting the boat count to tell them something comforting. Han arrived carrying last month's account and asked whether the new gate had already made them rich enough to repay him. Pei handed him the corrected list. He smiled at Yue's first mistake without mocking it, which made her more determined to keep the second column honest.

canal_p07_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_003.text: Last month's ordinary gross had been eighteen copper. The same account spent eighteen on keeper duties, rented gear and repeated temporary checks around the failing gate. It had yielded no spare toll share. Han knew the number and hated what it did to his claim. His mother's repayment agreement took its share from actual eligible receipts after essential operation, not from every boat that moved. The debt had survived because good years and difficult years never gathered into the smooth stream he remembered being promised.

canal_p07_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_004.text: The new gate could reduce repeated patching and waiting work, but this review term still had temporary service costs. Its two-month ordinary operating budget and projected toll receipts were both thirty-six, recorded apart from the earmarked one hundred twenty. The paid archive passage belonged there. Yue placed actual dated receipts above the forecast rather than pretending two future months had already filled the box. Han asked when the new leaner schedule would begin. Luo said only after the present commission's closing checks.

canal_p07_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_005.text: The proposed later monthly schedule used a conservative eighteen in gross receipts. Keeper work and an actual private-gear lease would need eight; six would rebuild the maintenance reserve; four could serve Han's remaining claim. A dry month could postpone the share if actual receipts did not provide it. Han stared at the four as if it were an insult. Pei asked him whether a larger invented number would buy his winter food. He said no, then asked whether the public twenty-four payment could happen sooner.

canal_p07_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_006.text: That payment remained proposed for the sixteenth-day hearing. The archive and receiving comparisons now supported it, but the reserve keeper still needed the council's recorded authorization before handing over money. Ninety-six had already been assigned to repair. The other twenty-four would reduce the valid eighty to fifty-six if approved and paid. Han's deposit notice created urgency in his private business; it did not make him the keeper of the public box. Yue had to carry that distinction while seeing how frightened he was of losing his crane.

canal_p07_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_007.text: A private broker reached the market before noon with an offer to buy the future fifty-six-copper claim at a discount, contingent on the twenty-four payment happening. He valued it at forty now, payable after the assignment was checked. Han could choose that bargain if its terms suited him. The broker could receive only the claim Han actually held, with its toll limits and dry-period delays. He could not turn purchasing a slow debt into purchasing the canal that happened to carry the receipts.

canal_p07_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_008.text: The broker said he understood all that, then proposed a missed-payment charge. An Ru had not arrived to review a new agreement; Pei compared the original clause and found no such fee in the canal's obligation. Han could sell his existing right, but could not impose a new charge on the common receiver through a private side contract. The broker crossed out that line and lowered his offer. Han asked him to return after the hearing. He needed to decide which impatience he could afford to satisfy.

canal_p07_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_009.text: Tian heard of the offer and wanted Han to take it immediately. If he had cash, perhaps he would stop arguing about the bank. Han asked whether she would sell a month's sewing wages cheaply so people found her less troublesome. She said the old notice had tried to sell her hours without asking. He agreed that it had, then said it still did not give her his present decision. Yue watched them reach a truth that refused to make either person instantly generous.

canal_p07_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_010.text: At the market edge, the widow sold washed blankets and wondered whether Tian could hem one by evening. Tian had her own orders and offered the following day. The widow said she preferred sooner and would ask another seamstress. Yue expected Tian to feel hurt after their family-history conversation. Tian only checked the cloth's measurements so the next worker would receive a useful order. Ordinary friendship could survive somebody buying elsewhere. Yue wished public disputes allowed that simple freedom as easily as a blanket's unfinished edge.

canal_p07_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_011.text: A cargo carrier arrived at the counter with two receipt slips stuck together by sweat. One showed the canal toll; the other belonged to Han's private crane. The carrier wanted both put against the public repair contribution somebody told him was mandatory. No such contribution had been authorized. Luo kept the ordinary toll, and Han's clerk explained the separate loading service. The carrier had heard a proposal in the market as if it were already a fee. Yue wrote a clear correction for the landings before rumor gained a cash box.

canal_p07_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_012.text: The broker's assistant wanted to count that corrected private fee as canal gross, making the future claim look safer. Han stopped him. The crane workers' wages and maintenance came from its own receipts, and the loading plot remained private. Combining accounts might raise the sale price on paper, but would leave the current workers arguing over money already promised to them. Han's refusal surprised Tian. He looked irritated at the surprise. He was capable of protecting an actual obligation without yet agreeing to every new public plan.

canal_p07_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_013.text: A boat's cargo included small jars of fish sauce, and one cracked when the crew set the basket too close to the landing edge. The smell overtook the toll shelter before anybody saw the leak. Yue helped move the intact basket to level paving while the owner collected the broken jar behind a marked walking gap. Tian said it smelled like a dragon had eaten the market. Luo opened the shelter window. Pei kept the accounts covered against a splash rather than treating their importance as a reason never to laugh.

canal_p07_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_014.text: The owner asked to unload the remaining jars at Han's reduced private berth. Han checked the crane's current limit and offered the actual service rather than a free favor meant to repair his reputation. The owner accepted its price and kept the broken-jar loss separate. Yue watched the familiar gear work within its new smaller arc. The boat took longer to position, and its crew grumbled. A narrower honest wharf could still earn money, though it would not do so by pretending its correction had cost nobody anything.

canal_p07_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_015.text: At noon, the counter's actual receipts were modest but real. Pei matched each to a boat or valid current passage, while Luo checked the operating expense dates. Yue wanted to compare the busy morning with last month's average and announce a recovery. Pei asked for more days before calling an unusual market morning an ordinary month. Their future plan could use a conservative forecast with its uncertainty visible. The first dozen happy boats were not a season, however much everyone wanted them to be.

canal_p07_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_016.text: Han invited Yue to see the goods behind his eighty-copper claim, saying she had met his papers often enough. The old timber account was in a drawer, but his mother's remaining personal things occupied a small chest above it. He opened only the account drawer at first. Yue said she had not come to price his mother. He answered that people at the meeting sometimes did, calling her kind or greedy according to which total they preferred. His tone was quiet enough that Tian stayed outside the door.

canal_p07_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_017.text: The drawer held a small receipt for repairing his mother's winter boots. Han had kept it because the date matched the first cash installment returned from the canal. She spent part of that payment on the boots rather than more stock, after years of telling him repaired leather was sufficient. The public account could verify the installment. It could not tell Yue what relief had felt like in those boots. Han showed her the surviving soles from the personal chest only after asking whether she wished to see them.

canal_p07_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_018.text: Yue looked at leather softened around a narrow heel and imagined the woman stepping out of the store. Then she caught herself making the mother gentler because the object was small. Han said she could be severe with debtors and foolishly indulgent with geese, neither quality deciding the title clause. He closed the chest and returned to today's receivable. The customer still owed eight copper for delivered goods. If the payment reached him, it would belong to his private return plan, not to the canal's forecast.

canal_p07_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_019.text: A messenger brought news that the payment boat had missed its transfer because a road cart shed a wheel. The customer's acknowledgment remained valid, but the cash would arrive later. Han wrote the new expected carriage date and sent a paid reply through his ordinary private delivery account. The broker had offered a faster uncertain future at a discount. Yue could see why forty immediate copper tempted a man whose eight ordinary copper kept moving farther down the calendar. The temptation did not grant him new public rights.

canal_p07_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_020.text: Tian entered after Han asked whether she wanted to hear the actual broker terms. She did, and he showed her the crossed-out fee. She thanked him for rejecting it because the bank would have borne a charge he never held. He said his mother had disliked selling people promises no one could keep. Tian glanced toward the public notice outside, where he had done something close to that himself. He understood the look and did not try to use the remembered mother as a defense.

canal_p07_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_021.text: The counter received an offered damage bill from the household whose drain had cleared. Its two damp-board repairs came from different winters, with dates but no proof of every cause. Luo would place them in the hearing's loss folder separately from the title and repayment decision. Yue asked whether that meant waiting again. The householder said waiting with an open drain and a receipt accepted was different from waiting while people called the whole fault imaginary. She still wanted an answer, and her patience had an actual edge.

canal_p07_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_022.text: Bao completed the first ordinary follow-up on the gate cap. Its marked fastenings remained seated after the busy morning, and the strip's leakage stayed within service limits. He charged the check to the accepted repair shift, with the keeper's regular observations recorded separately. Jiang had left for her next scheduled local job, leaving the case in the assigned store. Yue could copy the reading but would not use the powered frame without the agreed operator. There was no emergency today to make an exception sound attractive.

canal_p07_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_023.text: At the lower landing, a fisher complained that reopened cargo traffic disturbed his morning nets. His current permission assigned evening setting below the towline, not the market's busiest hours. He had moved earlier while the lock was closed and forgot to change back. Luo showed him the actual permission and offered the next evening's tide estimate. He shifted his nets reluctantly. The gate's return was a benefit to many boats, and an inconvenience to one man who had enjoyed the quieter mornings.

canal_p07_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_024.text: Pei asked Tian to sit with her while the clerk prepared the hearing invitations. The daughter of the woman whose work had been attributed to a dead husband wanted her mother's correction read before any debt number. Han agreed if the seasonal completion and remaining monetary claim were both preserved. The speaker order grew from actual people instead of a neat succession of headings. Yue helped address the absent households' copies, including the reed cutter's chosen counter collection. A hearing could be public without requiring everyone to gather in the same yard.

canal_p07_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_025.text: The broker returned unexpectedly with a second offer: slightly more immediate cash if Han accepted a private guarantee against poor toll months. Han could owe that guarantee himself, but the households would not. Han asked for the proposal in writing and declined to sign at the counter. The broker called him indecisive. 'For once,' Tian said quietly, 'that might be useful.' Han almost smiled. Yue wondered whether she could learn to value the pause before it had already saved her from a mistake.

canal_p07_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_026.text: The proposed gear lease needed an actual service schedule from Han before four monthly copper could be named as an operating cost. He listed ordinary landing tasks, current safe limits and maintenance duties on his own property. The bank would not pay rent for a crane it could never use under the public timetable. Luo marked the two useful cargo intervals and the alternatives available if the gear stood out of service. The future account was becoming a contract that could fail in specific ways, which made it more credible.

canal_p07_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_027.text: Three remaining comparisons would prepare tomorrow's packet. Luo needed the current toll traffic matched to its actual payments; Bao needed the gate's new maintenance schedule priced against the old temporary work; Han wanted the broker's revised assignment terms checked before he answered. Pei would receive all three reports at the counter. Yue could follow the moving boats, follow the operating work or follow the private proposal. Each path would show a different reason the same eighty copper had become so difficult to finish paying.

canal_p07_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_028.text: Tian said she would bring the household invitations wherever Yue worked. Han kept his proposed private agreement under its own cover; Luo left the public toll book open at the counter. Bao waited by the gate with the old check schedule and a clean replacement sheet. Yue could choose which comparison to help complete before supper. None would authorize payment today. The choice would change the questions she carried into a hearing whose result would affect people she now knew well enough to disappoint.

canal_p07_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_029.text: The afternoon's work lay between actual boats, actual upkeep and an offer for somebody else's patience. Yue could match toll entries with Luo, compare maintenance costs with Bao or review Han's broker terms. Pei would assemble the reports without treating any one as the whole canal. The public reserve still held its proposed twenty-four payment, the gate still needed its ordinary checks, and Han still had to decide how much future income he would sell to ease a present private fear.

choices.text: Match actual toll entries with Luo.
Compare upkeep costs and changed jobs with Bao.
Read Han's proposed private broker terms.

canal_p07_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_030.text: Luo gave Yue the payment book and sent the counter clerk to the movement board. They would compare every fresh receipt against an actual passage before the cash box was closed. A pilot's mark appeared twice, once for his boat and once for a later handcart crossing. Yue nearly merged them because the names matched. Luo pointed to the service columns. The man had used two different paid routes, each entered under its own rule. Neatness would have erased one actual service.

canal_p07_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_031.text: An empty cargo boat paid the same posted navigation toll as a loaded one because the fee concerned its lock passage. A child riding with its pilot added no passenger charge under the current rule. Yue asked why the clerk had left a small blank beside the child count. He said earlier drafts considered a different fee that was never approved. The blank was an obsolete form space, not evidence of somebody collecting a secret toll. She marked the current form for replacement at its next printing.

canal_p07_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_032.text: A landing porter brought a canceled receipt and its matching refund entry. His cargo turn had been moved upstream before the gate reopened. Yue checked the returned amount against the box and the date. The fresh gross list had counted the original payment without its cancellation. They corrected the net actual receipt before forecasting anything from it. The porter said he had come because he remembered being blamed for a clerk's missing refund years ago. Today he wanted both sides of the paper kept together.

canal_p07_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_033.text: The box held the expected coins after that correction. Luo still asked the clerk to read the count aloud while Yue matched the accepted entries. No hidden money appeared, and no public accusation was needed to make the ordinary task matter. A boatman waiting outside said officials looked disappointed when a box came out right. Yue smiled at the truth of it. She had imagined finding a dramatic discrepancy would prove she was helping. Instead she had helped prevent one from being invented.

canal_p07_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_034.text: At the landing, Yue watched actual cargo dwell time while Luo timed the gate cycle. A lighter boat passed quickly; a broad basket load needed careful positioning within the reduced private crane arc. The later monthly gross estimate stayed conservative because improved gate movement did not remove every constraint. Han's workers still had their own safe loading pace. Yue put the handling interval beside the navigation interval instead of calling every delay a failure of the public gate. The account began to describe a real working day.

canal_p07_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_035.text: A cloth seller asked whether a larger donation could buy her priority at the lock. Luo explained the current order and declined the conditional gift. The seller wanted a dependable shipping time more than generosity, and she appreciated hearing the actual alternative berth. Yue carried the untouched coin pouch back to her stall. The canal's proposed reserve could not become a price for entering ahead of neighbors. The seller booked a quieter departure rather than leaving with a private favor disguised as support.

canal_p07_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_036.text: An ordinary walker crossing the upper path found a loose flat coin near the counter step. Nobody could identify it from the payment list. The clerk put it in the landing's found-property envelope with the time and place, rather than adding it to toll gross because it lay conveniently close. Yue thought the envelope looked absurdly elaborate for one coin. Luo said the habit became harder to invent when a whole pouch appeared. The walker accepted the simple receiving note and went on.

canal_p07_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_037.text: Tian brought invitations while Yue worked and asked what the morning's boats proved. Yue said the actual current receipts were correct and the new cycle saved time under its checked ordinary conditions. They did not yet prove fourteen future payable months. Tian wanted the hearing to give Han an ending so the bank could stop returning to his claim. Yue showed her the dry-period clause. The end would arrive through actual payments, and a drought could move it. Tian disliked that answer but kept it in the invitation explanation.

canal_p07_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_038.text: The pilots' report gave the new gate a favorable ordinary trial and preserved two current delays unrelated to its repair. Luo accepted it without promising that winter ice would behave like an autumn market morning. Pei received the cash reconciliation and the outdated blank-form note. Yue returned the movement board to the clerk with its duplicated names still carrying separate services. She had spent an afternoon counting things that remained stubbornly individual. The sum was more dependable because it never pretended to know their whole future.

canal_p07_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_039.text: At dusk, Yue watched the final market boat leave with its owner standing beside the line. The day's corrected receipts went into the actual operating account. The conservative future toll schedule stayed a proposal, awaiting tomorrow's further comparisons and the sixteenth-day hearing. Luo thanked her for catching the canceled-payment error before the forecast grew around it. Yue said the porter had brought the missing connection. She wanted him named in the report, because the useful question had come from somebody remembering an earlier mistake.

canal_p07_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_040.text: Bao laid last month's temporary gate-check list beside the planned later service sheet. Repeated waiting and shaving had used ordinary paid work that a sound cap might reduce. The new schedule still required keeper observations, regular fastening checks and a repair reserve. Yue asked him how much they could safely remove. He wanted the earliest future month to retain extra checking after the first wet cycles. The leaner eight-copper operating plan would start only after the commission's actual closing evidence supported it, not simply because the new timber looked good.

canal_p07_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_041.text: Two temporary check workers came to hear the proposed schedule. One welcomed fewer cold nights at the gate; the other needed those wages and asked what work would replace them. Bao did not claim that the repair automatically created an equal new job. The new reserve would fund future tasks when needed, but it did not yet hire him. Yue hated how a successful repair could make an ordinary worker poorer. The man said he hated it too, and wanted that consequence recorded before anyone celebrated the saved cost.

canal_p07_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_042.text: Han's proposed gear lease would retain several private loading tasks under its actual service intervals. The check worker had line experience and could apply, but Han had not offered him employment. Yue carried his interest to the wharf clerk without presenting it as a funded transfer already arranged. The worker said he would also ask the upstream landing. Two possible routes were more useful than a promise the bank could not pay. Bao kept his objection in the cost report, where the meeting could hear it directly.

canal_p07_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_043.text: The old temporary schedule had three entries labeled only 'additional observation.' Bao found the keeper's separate log and matched them to real high-head leakage checks. They were not invented wages. The later gate design reduced the need for that recurring temporary watching under ordinary flow, while retaining explicit high-water checks. Yue copied the actual condition beside each service instead of erasing the entries as obsolete. A saving would be credible only if the new plan showed what changed and what kind of weather could bring the work back.

canal_p07_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_044.text: They walked to the lock to time a current fastening check. Luo took her measuring stick, inspected the cap mark and showed the seam-reading point. The ordinary task fit within her keeper round at today's water level. Bao would inspect the joint again after the next scheduled interval rather than send a separate person every hour. The former check worker watched and said that looked reasonable on a dry afternoon. His warning about a night rise remained unanswered until the future high-water schedule was drawn.

canal_p07_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_045.text: Bao marked the night-rise trigger on the same sheet as ordinary service. A keeper would notify the appointed landing receiver and close cargo movement if the head passed its current checked limit. High-water response required a fresh work call with actual available staff and supplies. It would not quietly borrow the erased household pledge. Yue liked the clearer procedure until the check worker asked who paid that fresh call. Luo pointed to the future reserve, then admitted a major emergency could exceed it and need another authorized source.

canal_p07_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_046.text: A carpenter's boy asked Bao whether the new cap made the old gate immortal. Bao gave him the discarded split peg blank and asked what water did to wood over years. The boy said his father's bucket fell apart, which seemed decisive. Yue laughed and watched Bao show the ordinary fastening mark. The repair bought useful service and a future inspection point. It did not abolish wear. A reserve made sense because the gate would eventually need something again, even if today's fit was excellent.

canal_p07_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_047.text: The householder with the cleared drain joined them and asked whether her check could sit beside the gate round rather than wait for another complaint. Luo added the reachable cover and outlet mark to her agreed seasonal walk, with a clear report route if the joint seep returned. Bao kept the masonry follow-up distinct from routine viewing. The householder liked seeing her drain in the keeper's hand instead of under a forgotten platform. She still expected her loss bills to be heard, which nobody asked her to trade away for the new place.

canal_p07_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_048.text: Yue copied the cost comparison after every actual duty had a receiver. The later eight-copper operation forecast included the keeper allowance and the proposed private-gear lease. It excluded speculative industrial growth and invisible unpaid watchers. The temporary worker's possible lost wages stayed in the hearing packet. Bao read that sentence before signing. He said the canal could still choose the better repair, but should know whose difficult change was counted among its benefits. Yue felt the account become heavier without growing less correct.

canal_p07_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_049.text: At the counter, Bao gave Pei the old paid-check references, the new ordinary schedule and the unresolved future-employment question. Yue brought the check worker's permitted interest to Han's clerk, where it joined actual applications rather than a public promise. The proposed saving had gained practical conditions. When Tian arrived with invitations, Yue asked her to include the affected worker among people offered a speaking turn. His experience belonged in tomorrow's preparation even though he did not own a household on the bank.

canal_p07_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_050.text: Han set the broker's revised offer on his store table with two empty cups keeping its curled corners flat. Yue read only the agreement he offered for comparison. It assigned his remaining actual toll claim after the public payment, gave a discounted private price and added his personal guarantee against poor receipts. The broker had removed the charge against the common receiver. Han asked whether Yue thought forty copper now was foolish. She said she could compare terms, but his winter risks were not hers to price.

canal_p07_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_051.text: The buyer's agent appeared while they read and asked whether the broker's advance would settle his deposit. Han said no advance had been accepted or paid. The agent wanted a firm private return plan before leaving for the next market. Han showed him the possible twenty-four public loan payment, eight owed by his customer and sixteen he hoped to raise from surplus private goods. Each remained at its actual stage. The agent disliked the uncertainty, but the contract's repayment period had not disappeared because he preferred immediate cash.

canal_p07_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_052.text: Yue asked Han which goods he intended to sell. He showed her an unused smaller hoist and a stack of private spare planks, bought for a canceled store extension. Bao would inspect the hoist before a price was offered. Selling them might raise the intended sixteen while keeping the repaired main crane working. Han did not own enough surplus to pretend the private decision painless. The unused extension had been his mother's plan for a larger shop, and he had kept its wood longer than the business justified.

canal_p07_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_053.text: The broker returned to explain the personal guarantee. If actual toll receipts fell, Han would make up the defined shortfall from his own listed private property under the new contract. It might be a lawful agreement, but it shifted dry-season risk onto the store. Han asked what happened if the same dry season reduced his private loading income. The broker said that was the reason for the discount and guarantee. His answer was unsentimental rather than hidden. Yue saw Han stop imagining the immediate forty as money without a future attached.

canal_p07_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_054.text: Han asked for a version without the guarantee. The broker offered less immediate cash, still with the original toll limits intact. Yue checked that the public receiver's obligation remained unchanged in both alternatives. Han could not transform a disappointing offer into evidence that the buyer was stealing from him. The broker was pricing delay. Han was pricing his own need for money today. They were finally bargaining over an object that existed, and its honest shape made the choices no easier.

canal_p07_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_055.text: Tian brought the household invitations while the broker waited outside. Han asked her whether she still wanted him to accept. She said she wanted the claim to stop controlling the bank's conversations, but had heard the personal guarantee and understood why he hesitated. He thanked her for revising the opinion. Yue noticed how little tenderness the exchange needed to count as a change. Tian did not forgive the sold-service notice. Han did not demand forgiveness before showing her the real private terms.

canal_p07_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_056.text: The broker offered to leave both versions for a day. Han accepted the papers and declined to sign during the meeting preparations. The buyer's agent warned that his own security date would still arrive at the term's end. Han nodded. He would seek an inspected price for the surplus goods and wait for the customer's actual eight copper before choosing a discounted assignment. Yue copied the two private alternatives into his offered comparison note. A decision postponed for specific evidence differed from one postponed because nobody wanted to see its costs.

canal_p07_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_057.text: A store worker asked whether selling the smaller hoist would remove his occasional private shift. Han said the canceled extension had supplied no regular work for months. The main crane and its actual shifts would remain if the deposit was returned through the current plan. The worker wanted that recorded before he recommended a possible purchaser. Han agreed and asked him to make the introduction only if he chose. The private settlement could use an employee's knowledge without claiming the employee owed a successful sale.

canal_p07_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_058.text: The worker recommended a cooper upriver whose small yard might use the inspected hoist. Han paid the ordinary private message fare and sent the dimensions, asking for a visit after the hearing. Yue did not add a sale receipt to the return plan. She added a contact and proposed inspection. Han watched her write the cautious stage and said he knew she was right but wished the columns would hurry. She remembered the dry gate waiting for its stone guide and said she understood that wish now.

canal_p07_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_059.text: Yue brought Pei only the offered comparison of the claim's actual toll limits; Han's private guarantee choices stayed under his own cover unless he chose to present them. At the counter, Tian was addressing the last absent household invitation. Han remained in his store, with two unsent signatures and one newly sent sale inquiry. The broker's offer had given him a real alternative without settling what he would accept. Yue could carry that uncertainty into the hearing rather than speaking as if she had rescued him from it.

canal_p07_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_060.text: Pei assembled the afternoon's reports after market traffic thinned. The actual toll entries had been reconciled, the later maintenance forecast had receivers and conditions, and Han held revised private assignment alternatives. No branch of the comparison had authorized the public payment early. Luo put the hearing packet beneath the counter's dry cover and asked Yue to check the speaker notices once more. The most important unanswered questions now had people attached to them, which would make tomorrow's preparation livelier and the hearing harder.

canal_p07_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_061.text: On the fifteenth morning, the temporary check worker visited the upstream landing. It offered two occasional private cargo shifts next month, with no standing appointment yet. He told Tian she could record the actual offer and his continued uncertainty. He would still speak about losing repeated gate-check wages. Yue liked that he refused to let a small improvement cancel the difficulty. The repaired canal could gain reliability while someone gained less income from it. A hearing that heard both facts might still choose repair, and would do so with open eyes.

canal_p07_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_062.text: The broker sent Han a note keeping the offer valid until the eighteenth day. Han had time to hear the council's actual payment decision, but the note would not wait indefinitely. Bao arranged an inspection of the unused hoist on that same later day within Han's private paid work. Its sale price remained unpromised. The private customer confirmed that his eight copper had been put onto a booked boat. Yue wrote the expected arrival separately from its receipt, remembering how often a journey became longer once money was in it.

canal_p07_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_063.text: Luo opened the counter for the morning's ordinary traffic before anybody rehearsed a speech. One boat's hauling line had tangled around a basket handle, delaying the cycle. The pilot cleared it from his safe standing position after the keeper held the gate still. Yue kept walkers out of the working corner. Nothing dramatic broke, and the ordinary current limit held. The delay still belonged in the timed record. Their repaired canal would always contain boats handled by people whose baskets and ropes had opinions of their own.

canal_p07_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_064.text: Tian tried reading the hearing's opening statement to Yue and made Han sound like the cause of every damp board on the bank. Yue showed her the separate drain evidence: platform access, a missing pin, roots at another joint and old public checks. Tian crossed out the line and looked furious at herself. She wanted the statement to be strong enough that nobody could dismiss the successor notice. Yue said its actual overreach was already strong. Borrowing every other grievance would make the truth easier to attack.

canal_p07_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_065.text: Tian rewrote the opening around the expired four annual seasons and the invalid sale of successor hours. She kept her anger in the sentence about people presently named, where it belonged. The daughter whose mother had worked under a dead husband's name would read her own correction. The householder would bring her actual damage bills. Yue would explain only the comparisons she had helped check. Their statements grew shorter as they became more precise, leaving time for people whose voices had not been included in the first draft.

canal_p07_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_066.text: Han prepared his own statement beside the private store window. He began with his mother's generosity, then crossed out a description of household ingratitude. The completed work certificate would make that claim unfair even if he still felt abandoned. He wrote the valid eighty-copper balance and the proposed twenty-four payment instead. Yue saw the discarded sheet when he showed her the finished copy, with permission. The choice of words did not erase his hurt. It stopped hurt from becoming another authority over people who had finished what they owed.

canal_p07_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_067.text: A letter from the absent reed cutter arrived with his approved acknowledgment reference and one sentence for the hearing. He wanted present workers to be hired under actual current tasks. He did not want his mother described as lucky to have been allowed to work. Pei checked the wording he offered and left it intact. Tian wanted to read it herself, but the letter asked for the clerk. She accepted the named speaker. A public voice could travel in writing without becoming a convenient line for someone else's performance.

canal_p07_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_068.text: Pei reviewed the scratched-through entry request before posting it beside the hearing notice. No matching counterfoil had arrived yet. The accepted seasonal total remained complete, and that single missing name would not hold up the old pledge's discharge. The request could continue after the hearing under its actual reference. Yue realized she had been hoping every uncertainty would close before the room gathered. Pei said public work often proceeded with a narrow question still open, provided nobody enlarged the question into a reason to keep an invalid power.

canal_p07_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_069.text: The householder brought her damp-board bills in a tin that once held sweets. Her youngest child asked whether the hearing would make the house smell new again. She said new boards had their own smell, and she wanted dry ones. Yue kept the offered copies in the loss folder, preserving their dates and leaving claimed causes separate. The drain's actual repair would be acknowledged tomorrow. The winter losses still needed evaluation. The tin made the claim look both smaller and more personal than the phrase 'consequential damages' ever had.

canal_p07_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_070.text: An Ru arrived that afternoon on the ordinary booked passage. The public operating account covered her official comparison travel within its existing budget. She took the archive extract from the clerk's cover and checked it against the receiving findings before hearing anyone's proposed conclusion. Pei offered her warm tea. Yue offered the report stack. An Ru chose the tea first because she had just carried the stack herself from the boat. They laughed, and the bank became a little less afraid of her careful questions.

canal_p07_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_071.text: She confirmed that the monetary balance and collective completed labor described different obligations. The title finding excluded the canal bed and successors' hours from Han's sale. The current notice would need a formal removal decision and the permitted monetary repayment its own resolution. Yue had heard these facts repeatedly, but the hearing would turn them into actual recorded actions. An Ru asked who would retain the amended originals afterward. The clerk named the public office and Han's own receiving copy, with the archive originals staying where they belonged.

canal_p07_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_072.text: The later gear lease still needed Han's final offered service schedule and the council's acceptance. Its proposed four monthly copper would support actual private services under current safe limits. An Ru noted that a debt share and a gear lease could be paid to the same person without becoming the same obligation. If the crane failed, the lease terms could change while the valid remaining loan did not vanish. Yue wrote that distinction for the keeper's later operating note, where it would matter when convenience stopped helping.

canal_p07_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_073.text: At the yard, Bao checked the hearing awning's ropes because a steady breeze had begun pulling one corner loose. Tian and the newer applicant lowered that side from the safe ground position while he refastened its ordinary tie. The repair crew's tools were stored, so they used the household awning kit with its owner present. Nobody called the task a fresh inherited workday. It took a few minutes and belonged to preparing a meeting they had chosen to attend, with no loaded gate hanging above them.

canal_p07_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_074.text: A child found Yue's first wrong cap chalk mark on the discarded scrap board and asked whether it was a secret cultivation sign. Yue said it was a wrong measurement line caught before cutting. The child looked disappointed, then asked if she could have the board for a game. Bao approved the clean offcut after checking its surface for nails. Yue watched the child draw three crooked gates over her failed line. Some mistakes could leave useful wood behind without requiring a ceremonial lesson.

canal_p07_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_075.text: At supper, Luo told An Ru that the gate worked and the drain emptied. She also told her the temporary check worker's hours would shrink, the food stall had lost sales and Han's customer paid extra to unload upstream. An Ru listened without asking why the successful repair sounded troubled. A public improvement brought changed costs as well as changed benefits. The hearing could establish the present truth without claiming that every person should feel relieved. Yue ate slowly, hearing the keeper choose honesty over a prettier report.

canal_p07_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_076.text: Han came after supper to confirm he would attend before the posted payment vote. Tian said the successor-lot statement came first, and he agreed to that order. He would not sign a private broker assignment tonight. Yue saw how much restraint the sentence required from a man carrying two deadlines. Outside, the buyer's agent checked his own departure booking. Nobody had become friends. Several people had become able to hear an action without mistaking it for surrender, which seemed more useful to tomorrow's yard.

canal_p07_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_077.text: Yue made her personal practice check on an unpowered comparison tile before putting it away. Her recovered sensation matched the earned second pair. There was no reason to open another route on the strength of a well-counted account. She wanted progress in cultivation as much as ever, but today she could name a different progress too: correcting the token entry, waiting for cash still on a boat, and helping Tian remove an unfair accusation without demanding that she lose her anger.

canal_p07_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p07_078.text: The hearing chairs waited beneath the secured awning. Pei placed the receiving schedule where its broad columns could be read; An Ru set the certified original terms beside it. The clerk left room for the proposed payment and the formal canceled-sale finding. Yue stood at the gate before sleeping, watching its wet cap beneath the lantern. On the sixteenth morning, they would decide what could be repaid, what could never have been sold and what work people would be asked to choose next.
